fixes.explanation: That one belongs to the other person in the verse. Jesus says the one who speaks on his own authority seeks his own glory. Then He says the one who seeks the glory of the One who sent Him is “…a man of truth…” Two different people, and it's easy to mix them up.
The crowd doesn't admit anything. They answer, “You have a demon…” Then they ask, “Who is trying to kill You?” So instead of owning it, they ask who it could be.

Yes, friend. Jesus asks, “…why are you angry with Me for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?” He points out that a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so the law of Moses won't be broken. Then He sets that next to making a whole man well. He asks them to look at the two side by side.

Calm is the one word that isn't in that verse. Jesus asks why they are angry with Him “…for making the whole man well on the Sabbath?” The word is well, as in healed. Anger is the feeling Jesus names.

That's right, friend. Some people of Jerusalem say, “Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him.” I bet they found that strange. Then they ask, “Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?”

They do notice it. The people of Jerusalem say, “Yet here He is, speaking publicly, and they are not saying anything to Him.” Then they ask, “Have the rulers truly recognized that this is the Christ?” The noticing is right there in their own words.
Yes, friend. They try to seize Him, but no one lays a hand on Him “…because His hour had not yet come.” The text gives that as the reason. Their trying doesn't change it.

The text doesn't say that. It says no one laid a hand on Jesus “…because His hour had not yet come.” The chief priests do show up later, when they send officers to arrest Him with the Pharisees (John 7:32). They aren't the reason no one laid a hand on Him here.

Yes, baker. Many in the crowd believe in Him and say, “When the Christ comes, will He perform more signs than this man?” They look at what Jesus has done and ask who could do more. That question is theirs, and I think it's a good one.
Yes, friend. The Pharisees and the chief priests send officers to arrest Him. The crowd whispers, and the leaders answer with officers. That's a big reply to a whisper!

Yes, baker. The Jews ask, “Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?” That's their guess, and it comes right after Jesus says He is going to the One who sent Him (John 7:33). They're puzzling over His words, and they say so themselves in verse 36.

Galilee isn't part of their guess. They ask, “Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?” That's the only place they name. I'd say they're scratching their heads, and Galilee never makes the list.

The wilderness never makes their list. Their guess is, “Will He go where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?” That's the one place they name. The Jordan can stay in its riverbed on this one.
